co_witches_tower.blurb: Witches' Tower is a compact granite buttress in Boulder Canyon, a short way up the creek from the highway and easy to mistake for part of the hillside. It holds thirteen lines: bolted and gear-protected sport and trad routes from the high 5.8s through the low 5.12s, plus three boulder problems that run from very easy to very hard. The steep west side carries the bolted lines, while the north side is lower in angle, lichenous and shadier. Expect gritty, sometimes loose rock, a creek to cross on the way in, and a quieter feel than the canyon's roadside crags.

co_pitch_penny_boulder.blurb: Pitch Penny Boulder is a single freestanding block at the north end of Rotary Park, on the Horsetooth side of Fort Collins. Thirteen problems are recorded, mostly easy-to-moderate lines from V0 up to about V5, plus a couple of much harder V7 lines. The south side is well featured with short, friendly problems, while the smoother west side asks for more technical movement and feels easier in cool, cloudy conditions. Landings are soft and sandy, so a pad is optional, though the dirt at the base of the south face is eroding and slippery on the walk-off. Expect passing hikers and dogs.

co_central_park_bouldering_area.blurb: This is a small, man-made bouldering wall in Denver's Central Park, in the Stapleton neighborhood, designed to look like natural boulders. It stretches roughly thirty feet and stands eight to twelve feet tall, with wood chips underfoot. Thirteen problems are listed, from very easy up to V8, with a good share of traverses in the V5 to V6 range, so there is enough to keep a stronger climber busy and a few easy lines for newcomers. The walk from the car is under a minute, which makes it a handy spot for a quick after-work session or a training top-up in the city.

co_ufc_wall.blurb: UFC Wall is a northwest-facing sandstone wall deep in Devil's Canyon, in the McInnis Canyons area near Fruita and Grand Junction. Thirteen routes are listed, almost all traditional, running from about 5.8 to 5.11 and dominated by off-width and chimney climbing, so bring wide gear and a taste for grappling. The rock is better than much of the canyon, and the wall stays shaded until the afternoon for most of the year. The catch is the approach: about four miles each way up the canyon, committing enough that this is a full day out rather than a quick lap session.
